decisions.reason: A classic lever handle close to the core range costs little to keep in the catalogue, and one year on the market reveals too little to justify abandoning the option.
A lever handle family shares production and distribution with the established offer, so it is cheap to hold while architects' project specifications build up.
Its uncertainty about design acceptance is still unresolved after only a year, and keeping it within a broad portfolio costs little.
Like other new handle designs, it is a low-cost option whose value in long project-specification cycles is not yet revealed.
A handle family supports the firm's push toward system breadth, and there is no evidence yet that its value will not be realized.
The electronic access system with its distinctive light technology is a strategic growth option in digital building organization, so it merits further commitment rather than abandonment.
